name: Garig-Ilgar
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible
sweep_summary: Garig-Ilgar (gari1253) is not in the catalog. Both works with stress in the title (Weinberger & Kunath 2011; Weinberger 2015, the Speech Accent Archive) are Glottolog computerized 'archive'-keyword assignments (language code field reads 'computerized assignment from \"archive\"' in the local Glottolog 5.1 sources.bib) and concern L2 English accents; not relevant. ~110 of the 120 Glottolog entries attached to this language are the same kind of keyword noise. No first-hand statement of Garig/Ilgar word-stress placement was found in any open text: the only Ilgar-specific stress remark located is in Evans 2000 'Kinship verbs' (archive.org snippets, borrow-only scan) and concerns classifier-vs-root prominence in kinship-verb compounds, not syllable placement. Sister-language statements exist for Iwaidja (Capell 1962 sec. 1.7: initial stress; Pym & Larrimore 1979 snippets; Caudal & Mailhammer 2022 downloaded open, intonation only). The likely authoritative sources remain unreachable by open routes: Evans 2000 Linguistic Typology overview (paywalled, no OA copy), Evans 2000 ms grammar (129 pp., not online), Evans & Wardaga 2003 dictionary, Mailhammer & Harvey 2018 (Newcastle handle dead). discovery ran through Glottolog, OpenAlex, Unpaywall, Crossref, archive.org FTS and direct downloads. All downloaded material and a dated record are in ( updated).

sources.citation: Hualde, José Ignacio and Nadeu, Marianna (2011). Lenition and phonemic overlap in Rome Italian. Phonetica 68. pp. 215-242.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: The paper is an acoustic study of intervocalic /p t k/ vs /b d g/ in ROME ITALIAN (Indo-European, Romance). The full 28-page text contains zero mentions of Garig, Ilgar, Iwaidja or Australia. It is attached to gari1253 in Glottolog only through the computerized keyword assignment 'rome'. Nothing in it bears on Garig-Ilgar word stress; the catalog has no record for gari1253 and this work adds none.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2007. Pseudo-argument affixes in Iwaidja and Ilgar: a case of deponent subject and object agreement. In M. Baerman, G. Corbett, D. Brown & A. Hippisley (eds), Deponency and morphological mismatches (Proceedings of the British Academy 145), 271-296.
sources.note: Only a passing remark, fn. 15 (p. 289), about an IWAIDJA verb: 'that stress is appropriately placed (e.g. primary stress on the putative root-initial in àngmárrangùldin)' -- i.e. main stress on the root-initial syllable after the prefix, with secondary stresses marked on prefix and later syllable. No statement for Ilgar/Garig. Fn. 2 gives the orthography and notes no phonemic voicing contrast.
sources.venue: Deponency and morphological mismatches (Proceedings of the British Academy 145)

sources.note: Iwaidja only: IP boundaries marked tonally and durationally, nucleus = 'alignment of a pitch accent with the head of a foot'; syllabification across word boundaries; no word-stress placement rule.

sources.citation: Pym, Noreen with Bonnie Larrimore. 1979. Papers on Iwaidja phonology and grammar. Work Papers of SIL-AAB A-2. Darwin: SIL.
sources.note: Full stress analysis for Iwaidja, the near-identical sister language (Garig/Ilgar are dialect-level relatives per Evans); archive.org scan is borrow-only, snippets confirm a word-stress section with stress-shift conditions.

sources.citation: Capell, Arthur. 1962. Some linguistic types in Australia (Handbook of Australian Languages, Part 2). Oceania Linguistic Monographs 7. Sydney: University of Sydney. Rosetta Project excerpt of the Jiwadja (Iwaidja) phonology pages.
sources.note: For JIWADJA (= Iwaidja, iwai1244), sec. 1.7 'Stress': 'Stress is normally on the first syllable of a di- or trisyllabic word; in four syllable words there is a secondary stress on the third syllable. In some disyllabic words and in longer words there is a trochaic rhythm built up based on initial stress, but occasionally final stresses are found, as in /ga'ralg/, "his body".' Not about Garig/Ilgar (Capell notes the Jiwadja phonemic system is 'practically the same as that of Maung').

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas, Bruce Birch, Judith Bishop, Ilana Mushin & Janet Fletcher. 1999. The sound of one quotation mark: intonational cues to quotation in five north Australian languages. Paper presented at ALS99, the 1999 Conference of the Australian Linguistic Society (University of Western Australia, Perth); abstract in 'ALS99 Abstracts: E-L', Australian Linguistic Society website.
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: An instrumental study of INTONATION, not lexical tone - reports 'the main intonational cues associated with quotative framing, most notably, pitch reset and top line pitch movements' in Iwaidja and Ilgar narrative, plus polyphonic base lines for represented dialogue; pitch is treated as post-lexical (intonational); the abstract makes no claim about lexical tone or word stress in Ilgar. Listed because it is the only located prosodic study that uses Ilgar data at all.

tone.quote: The present paper reports on preliminary analyses of intonational framing of quoted speech in five non-Pama-Nyungan languages: Mayali and Dalabon (both Gunwinyguan), Iwaidja and Ilgar (both Iwaidjan) and Kayardild (Tangkic). In the main body of the paper we survey the main intonational cues associated with quotative framing, most notably, pitch reset and top line pitch movements.
tone.locator: ALS99 Abstracts E-L web page, first abstract (no pagination)

Listed because it is the only located prosodic study that uses Ilgar data at all.
